findings.basis: Real carrier settings, in four groups. (1) Google CarrierSettings: att_us, dish5gsa_us, optus_au and starhub_sg set false. The Dish5Gsa profiles on 208-09 and 302-220 are Google's dish5gsa_us IMSI-range entries from a newer Pixel carrier list (blazer). M1 is Google's m1_sg in the Pixel vendor baseline (barbet). (2) AOSP CarrierConfig: AT&T, Cricket, FirstNet, OXIO, NTT Docomo and Aio set false. The OXIO profile matches carrier ID 2652. (3) LineageOS device overlays: carrier-scoped false blocks for Orange FR, Telekom DE, KT, SKT, LG U+, China Mobile, Unicom, Telecom and Broadnet, Digi MY, Globe PH and Seatel, found in many OEM trees. (4) Sony's carrier blocks for the AT&T PLMNs. For 310-280, 310-380, 310-410, 505-02 and 525-05 the Google lane already serves false. For the rest it serves the default true.
findings.effect: With false, TelephonyConnectionService hangs up every other TelephonyConnection and conference before it places the emergency call, with cause OUTGOING_EMERGENCY_CALL_PLACED. It does not hold them (TelephonyConnectionService.java:2392-2408; the same in recreateEmergencyConnection, 3544-3559). Telecom's CallSequencingController also disconnects ongoing managed calls whose account carries false, instead of leaving them to be held (CallSequencingController.java:1016-1037, 1097-1100; CallsManager.java:4623-4647 defaults a missing key to true). The hangup marks the ImsPhoneCall DISCONNECTING at once (ImsPhoneCall.onHangupLocal). DISCONNECTING is not 'alive' (Call.java:53-55), so ImsPhoneCallTracker.checkForDialIssues does not block the dial, and prepareForDialing skips the hold-before-dial step (ImsPhoneCallTracker.java:1665-1694, 2716-2734). The emergency call is dialled at once. The ImsStack and its OCD fork do not read the key. With the default true, the tracker first holds the active call, then dials. If that hold fails, prepareForDialing throws 'cannot dial in current state' (ImsPhoneCallTracker.java:1683-1686), and the emergency call must fall back.
findings.risk: No added risk to the emergency call. With false, the 112 call never waits on a hold transaction that can fail. The cost falls on the other call, which is dropped instead of held: the user cannot return to it after the emergency call. Google already ships this behaviour for AT&T, Optus, StarHub and Dish, so it is a normal platform path. TTY, RTT and WPS calls are not touched. Read in the 23.2 tree. The phone runs 24.0, where these paths are not expected to change; not re-checked.

notes: Proceed for all 52 profiles. False makes the platform drop, rather than hold, other calls when an emergency call starts. That is the more direct path for the emergency call itself: no hold step that can fail and block the dial. Every value traces to a real carrier-scoped setting from Google, AOSP or OEM carrier overlays. The key stays in group A, because it changes what happens to calls when an emergency call is placed.
